reasoning:
Key conflict: R1 says queue_sms exists with attribute access; R3 says sent_messages returns dicts and only send_sms exists. R3 is the corrected, re-verified finding — the researcher explicitly re-checked and says the codebase has send_sms(phone, text) with dict records, and no SmsMessage construction. R1's claim about queue_sms conflicts with tests? Actually R1 says tests are authoritative for queue_sms... but R3 re-checked and found only send_sms. Hmm. R1 says "the copy of notifications/sms.py I could read exposes only send_sms... which conflicts with the tests and core/models.py; the tests and models (queue_sms...) are authoritative." R3 re-verified and says sent_messages is list[dict], no SmsMessage construction, no queue_sms found in codebase search. R3 is the later, more careful finding. The safest plan: use send_sms(phone, text) with the original's phone and text — that satisfies "same message and details" since text is rendered already in the outbox line. R5 says resend should reuse phone, text, household_id, template_id, params with new id and queued_at. send_sms only takes phone and text; the outbox line written by send_sms has keys id, phone, text, queued_at (per R3). But R5 says existing lines have household_id, template_id, params too. Hmm — R5 says existing lines have that shape. If send_sms writes only id/phone/text/queued_at, then existing lines wouldn't have household_id... but R5 observed they do. Contradiction again.

Given the ambiguity, the plan should handle it: read the outbox via sent_messages() (dicts per R3), filter ids where delivery_status() == 'failed', and for each, call send_sms(m['phone'], m['text']). That reuses existing function, appends new lines with fresh ids via next_number/format_sms_id internally. The "same message" is the text. If send_sms doesn't carry household_id/template_id/params, we can't add them without editing sms.py. Should we plan a step to modify notifications/sms.py to add queue_sms? The tests are authoritative per R1 and expect queue_sms with household_id, template_id, params, MAX_LENGTH=140, sms_ok check. But R3 says the codebase only has send_sms. If tests test queue_sms, tests would fail currently... The researcher says tests are authoritative. Hmm, but R3's codebase-wide search found no SmsMessage construction or import — meaning sms.py doesn't use it. Tests use attribute access m.id on sent_messages() results, which wouldn't work on dicts. So tests would fail. This suggests sms.py needs to be updated to match tests: implement queue_sms, SmsMessage records.

But the ticket ask is just a script. Minimal approach: plan one step to update notifications/sms.py to match the authoritative tests (add queue_sms returning SmsMessage, sent_messages returning SmsMessage objects, MAX_LENGTH=140), then a step for the script using queue_sms(household_id, template_id, params) reusing original details, then a step to run it. That satisfies "same message and details as the original" fully (household_id, template_id, params reused; text re-rendered via render — same text since template approved and params same).

Alternatively, avoid touching sms.py: script uses send_sms(m['phone'], m['text']). That texts the same phone with the same text — "same message and details as the original" arguably satisfied at the message level. But R5 explicitly says a resend should reuse household_id, template_id, params too. With send_sms we can't. Hmm, but R5 describes the existing line shape; maybe send_sms does write those? R3 says "the keys written by send_sms()" include household_id, phone, text, template_id, params, queued_at — actually R3 lists: "m['id'], m['household_id'], m['phone'], m['text'], m['template_id'], m['params'], m['queued_at'] — the keys written by send_sms()". So send_sms writes all those keys! Wait, R3 says send_sms(phone, text) but the keys written include household_id, template_id, params? That's odd but R3 explicitly lists them as "the keys written by send_sms()". Hmm, re-read: "callers must access fields as dict keys (m['id'], m['household_id'], m['phone'], m['text'], m['template_id'], m['params'], m['queued_at'] — the keys written by send_sms())". So the outbox records contain all those keys. But send_sms signature only takes phone and text... contradiction within R3. Unless send_sms looks up household from phone? Unclear.

Given the mess, safest plan that satisfies the done-when: script reads outbox dicts, filters failed ids via delivery_status(), and for each failed message calls send_sms(m['phone'], m['text']). New ids generated by send_sms. Nobody delivered is texted. That works regardless of whether queue_sms exists. But if tests require queue_sms... the ticket doesn't ask to fix sms.py.

Actually, wait — maybe better to reconcile: R1 says tests are authoritative and queue_sms exists in tests. R3 re-verified the implementation. The planner should rely on findings; R3 is the most recent re-check. I'll go with send_sms approach but note reusing phone and text from the original outbox record. Also optionally audit per R10? Optional; keep it simple but R10 says "may follow this pattern if it audits" — I could include an audit append. Keep it: append audit entry per resend using store.append_jsonl. That's reasonable but optional; I'll include it as part of the script step.
